fixes.explanation: True, friend. The psalm says, "…fruit trees and all cedars…" (Psalm 148:9) The trees get a spot on the list, right along with the mountains and the hills. Fruit trees and all the cedars, together in one verse.

Right at the top, the psalm says, "Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise Him in the highest places." (Psalm 148:1) The psalm writer starts way up high and works his way down. By verse 7 he gets to the ground: "Praise the LORD from the earth…" (Psalm 148:7)

The temple is a fair guess, friend. But the psalm doesn't start there. It says, "Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise Him in the highest places." (Psalm 148:1) The writer is looking way up before he looks anywhere near a building.

Prophets are a fair guess, but they aren't in this verse. Up in the heavens, the psalm says, "Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His heavenly hosts." (Psalm 148:2) The angels are the first ones called on.

Priests are a fair guess, so I see why you picked them. But this part of the psalm is still up in the heavens, and it says, "Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His heavenly hosts." (Psalm 148:2) Angels get the first call, not priests.

That's the reason, friend. The psalm says, "Let them praise the name of the LORD, for He gave the command and they were created." (Psalm 148:5) He spoke, and they were made, sun, moon and stars included. I can't even get my dough to rise when I ask nicely.

Priests and Levites are a fair guess. But the psalm doesn't name them here. When it gets to people, it says, "…kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all rulers of the earth…" (Psalm 148:11) Rulers come first.
Mercy is a lovely thing to praise Him for, friend. But this psalm gives a different reason: "…for His name alone is exalted…" (Psalm 148:13) That's what the writer points to here.
